1. What is ChatGPT?
ChatGPT is an AI chatbot developed by OpenAI, capable of generating human-like responses in natural language.

2. Is ChatGPT free to use?
Yes, ChatGPT is free to use. However, OpenAI offers a subscription plan called ChatGPT Plus, which provides additional features and access to GPT-4 for $20/month.

3. Can I use OpenAI’s models via API?
Yes, developers can use OpenAI’s API to integrate language models into their own applications and services.

4. How does OpenAI ensure safety?
OpenAI employs moderation tools and model fine-tuning to reduce harmful and biased outputs. Additionally, they have implemented data controls that allow users to decide how their conversations are used.

5. What are the usage limits?
Free-tier users have usage caps, while ChatGPT Plus subscribers receive general priority access and higher usage limits.

1. Overview
This policy outlines the expectations, tools, and responsibilities for employees working remotely, either full-time or under hybrid arrangements.

2. Working Hours

Employees are expected to be available between 10:00 AM – 6:00 PM (IST), Monday through Friday.

Flexibility is allowed with prior manager approval.

All meetings must be attended unless a valid reason is communicated in advance.

3. Tool Access & Communication

3. Tool Access & Communication

Primary tools: Slack (messaging), Zoom (video), Notion (documentation), and Jira (task tracking).

Employees must check Slack at least once every hour during work hours.

Weekly standups via Zoom are mandatory on Mondays at 10:30 AM.

4. Performance Tracking

Work progress is tracked via Jira. Tasks must be updated daily.

KPIs will be evaluated bi-weekly in 1-on-1 meetings with team leads.

Deadlines must be respected unless escalated with justification.

5. Security Protocols

Use VPN when accessing company resources.

Do not use personal devices unless authorized.

All files must be stored in the company-approved cloud system (Google Drive/Notion).

Two-factor authentication (2FA) is mandatory for all tools.

6. Policy Violations
Failure to adhere to this policy may lead to formal warnings or revocation of remote privileges.

1. Pairing Your AirPods

With Apple Devices:
Open the AirPods case near your iPhone. A setup animation should appear on your iPhone screen. Tap "Connect" to begin the pairing process. Once set up with one Apple device, your AirPods connect automatically to your other Apple devices signed in to the same Apple ID.

With Non-Apple Devices:
Open the AirPods case, press and hold the setup button on the back until the status light flashes white. Then, go to the Bluetooth settings on your device and select your AirPods from the list.

2. Charging Your AirPods

Place your AirPods in the charging case and close the lid. The status light indicates the charge status.

Use a Lightning cable to charge the case. The LED light shows charging status.

3. Controls and Gestures

3. Controls and Gestures

Play/Pause Audio: Double-tap either AirPod.

Skip to Next Track: Double-tap either AirPod.

Activate Siri: Double-tap either AirPod.

You can customize these controls in the Bluetooth settings on your iPhone.

4. Using Siri

Activate Siri: Double-tap either AirPod. Then, you can ask Siri to perform tasks like playing music, making calls, or providing directions.

5. Resetting Your AirPods

5. Resetting Your AirPods

Place your AirPods in their case and close the lid. Wait 30 seconds, then open the lid.

Press and hold the setup button on the back of the case until the status light flashes amber, then white.

Reconnect your AirPods by placing them near your device and following the on-screen instructions.

1. What is GitHub Copilot?
GitHub Copilot is an AI pair programmer developed by GitHub and OpenAI. It helps you write code faster by suggesting entire lines or blocks based on natural language comments and the current code context.

2. How Does It Work?

Trained on billions of lines of public code from GitHub.

Uses OpenAI Codex (a descendant of GPT-3) to generate code suggestions.

Integrates directly into editors like Visual Studio Code.

3. Key Features

3. Key Features

Code Autocompletion: Suggests entire functions and repetitive code patterns.

Natural Language Input: You can write comments like // sort array and Copilot suggests code accordingly.

Support for Many Languages: Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Ruby, Go, and more.

4. Limitations

Not Always Right: Suggestions may not always work or follow best practices.

Security & Bias: May suggest insecure or biased code based on its training data.

Not a Replacement: It's a coding assistant, not a full AI developer.

5. FAQs

Is Copilot free?: Initially launched in technical preview; now available via GitHub Copilot subscription.

Can I use it for proprietary code?: It’s designed to assist, but generated code should be reviewed before use in production.

1. Battery & Range

Standard Range Plus: ~272 miles (EPA est.)

Long Range AWD: ~358 miles (EPA est.)

Performance Model: ~315 miles (EPA est.)

2. Performance

0–60 mph (Performance): 3.1 seconds

Top Speed (Performance): 162 mph

Drivetrain: Rear-wheel drive (Standard) or Dual motor all-wheel drive (Long Range & Performance)

3. Autopilot & Self-Driving

Autopilot: Standard with lane keeping and adaptive cruise control

Full Self-Driving (FSD) Capability: Optional upgrade including Navigate on Autopilot, Auto Lane Change, Autopark, Summon, and Traffic Light/Stop Sign Control

4. Safety & Ratings

Crash Rating: 5-Star Overall Rating from NHTSA

Safety Features: Emergency braking, collision warning, blind-spot monitoring, lane departure warning

5. Interior & Tech

Touchscreen: 15” central touchscreen

Connectivity: Wi-Fi, LTE, navigation, video streaming (YouTube, Netflix)

Seats: All vegan interior with heated seats

6. Charging

Compatible with Tesla Supercharger network

Home charging via NEMA 14-50 or Tesla Wall Connector
